By the end of the night, a further 21 players had punched their tickets to Day 2 and locked up at least a min-cash. Day 1c attracted 137 entries, while the ongoing Day 1d Turbo flight added a further 67 after late registration came to a close. That brought the total field size to 507 entries, with a maximum of 76 players set to return for Day 2, all guaranteed a share of the $5,000,000 prize pool . Geoffrey Mooney was the only player to qualify twice and has therefore secured himself a min-cash, bringing his biggest stack forward. Ending at the top for the night was Artsiom Lasouski , who bagged 2,180,000 to become the overall chip leader through the first three flights and the only player to surpass the two-million-chip mark. Kadir Altinbasak finished second with 1,630,000, while Andrey Pateychuk rounded out the podium positions with 1,200,000. Day 1c Top Ten Chip Counts Rank Player Country Chip Count Big Blinds 1 Artsiom Lasouski Belarus 2,180,000 109 2 Kadir Altinbasak Turkey 1,630,000 82 3 Andrey Pateychuk Russian Federation 1,200,000 60 4 Boris Kolev Bulgaria 1,105,000 55 5 Danilo Velasevic Serbia 965,000 48 6 Aleksejs Ponakovs Latvia 920,000 46 7 Maksym Mamon Russian Federation 870,000 44 8 Italo Modena Italy 625,000 31 9 Maksim Shornikau Belarus 620,000 31 10 Ignat Liviu Romania 575,000 29 Jamil Wakil Lasouski was in from the start, and although his first bullet didn't go according to plan, his second proved much more successful. He had already built one of the biggest stacks in the room by the time registration closed before pulling away from the rest after sending Jamil Wakil to the rail. Lasouski then hit a set of deuces to bust Xiaosheng Zheng near the money, helping him become the man to catch for Day 2. Many new players, or those having another shot at building a stack, were on the felt throughout the day, with many falling short of the finish line. Among the notable names to hit the rail were Mehdi Chaoui , Felipe Ketzer , Daniel Rezaei , the 2019 WSOP Main Event champion Hossein Ensan , PLO end boss Eelis Parssinen , and Manig Loeser , who soft bubbled after running pocket jacks into two kings. Daniel Rezaei With the exit of Loeser and play now on the bubble, it didn't take long before Michael Allen shoved his incredibly short stack into the middle over a raise from Danilo Velasevic . Allen got it in good with ace-king suited, but he needed to hold against Velasevic's mighty queen-five offsuit. That wasn't to be, and Allen earned the unwanted title of bubble boy, and the remaining players bagged up with 34 minutes remaining in Level 15. Some other notable names returning to the baize for Day 2 include Boris Kolev (1,105,000), Aleksejs Ponakovs (920,000), Maksim Shornikau (620,000), Ignat Liviu (575,000), and Milad Oghabian (470,000), who doubled just a few spots from the money against the eventual chip leader. Also surviving were Alexey Borovkov (455,000), Oshri Lahmani (425,000), Patrick Brooks (310,000), and Fabian Schmidt (20,000), who returns with just one big blind remaining. Milad Oghabian Day 2 gets underway at 1 p.m. on Monday, August 10, when the survivors from the four opening flights will combine under one roof for the first time. Everyone returning is guaranteed a payday, with the official prize pool and payouts set to be announced shortly before cards hit the air. Blind levels will increase to 60 minutes, with the plan to play down until the final table is reached. https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/fid.text: The Budapest Times Fidesz hits back: Magyar should stop expecting others to do his job The prime minister should not always expect others to solve every government task — wrote the Fidesz communications director in a statement sent to MTI on Sunday, responding to remarks made by Péter Magyar in Paks concerning the corporate sector. Bertalan Havasi pointed out that Hungarian entrepreneurs are also taxpayers, meaning they “pitch in to the shared celebration.” Moreover, the previous national government had also brought multinational companies into the system of shared public burdens, he added. What would truly be “fair and right” is for Péter Magyar to stop speaking incoherently, and to stop always expecting others to solve every government task while blaming the previous government for his own incompetence — reads the statement from the Fidesz communications director. At a press conference in Paks on Sunday, Péter Magyar asked the corporate sector to support the seventieth anniversary celebrations on 23 October. The previous government had spent every available forint earmarked for such events. Only a few hundred million forints remained for 23 October, which is “outrageous,” the prime minister added.
